thread.title: Overnight Markets: US stocks end mostly lower as bond yields rise

title: Overnight Markets: US stocks end mostly lower as bond yields rise
text:
By Himanshu Singh 02 Feb, 2018 at 01:58 
Wall Street stocks closed mostly lower on Thursday after a midday gain faded by late afternoon as bond yields rose and technology stocks retreated ahead of a host of high-profile earnings. 
The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 37 points, or 0.14%, to 26,187, the S&P 500 lost two points, or 0.06%, to 2,822 and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 26 points, or 0.35%, to 7,386. 
Retailers, restaurant chains and other consumer-focused companies accounted for much of the market's pullback. The losses outweighed solid gains by financial stocks, which got a boost as climbing bond yields set the stage for higher interest rates on mortgages and other loans. 
Among the notable market movers, eBay (EBAY.O) gained 13.8% after its earnings report, and its announcement that it would move away from PayPal (PYPL.O) as its main payments partner. PayPal shares slid 8.1%. 
UPS (UPS.N) was down 6.1% after it reported fourth-quarter profit that was hurt by higher holiday season shipping costs. The company was the second-biggest percentage loser on the S&P 500. 
Qorvo led all gainers in the S&P 500, jumping 16.1%. Facebook rose 3.3% a day after the social media company posted strong quarter results. 
High-profile tech companies reported after the closing bell. Amazon.com (AMZN.O) was up over 6.0% in after hours trading after results. Alphabet (GOOGL.O) was down nearly 3.0% in extended trade after its quarterly earnings. Apple (AAPL.O) went down about 1.0% in after hours trading after posting results. 
In economic news, initial claims for US unemployment benefits were below expectations, indicating a tight labour market. 
In Asia, shares came under pressure early on Friday after Wall Street closed mixed and yields on US government debt rose in the last session. 
Japan's Nikkei 225 declined 0.75% after snapping a six-day losing streak in the previous session. Across the Korean Strait, the Kospi fell 0.96%. Down Under, the S&P/ASX 200 reversed early losses to edge higher by 0.2%. 
In Greater China, the Hang Seng Index declined 0.90%, while on the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.48%.
